# Behavioural Skills

> A catalogue of behavioural-science skills — markdown instruction files with
> declared inputs, outputs, and evidence bases — designed to be installed into
> AI coding agents. Install: `curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/scripts/install.sh | bash -s -- --target . --name <skill>`

## Skills

- [Choose Which AI Evaluations to Run Next](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/ai-eval-level-matcher/SKILL.md): Use when a team with an AI product for a social cause must decide which evaluation to run next, especially when a funder wants proof of impact. It recommends which of four stages the product is ready for (the AI model, the product, user behaviour, real-world impact) and says whether a randomized controlled trial is still too early. To design the chosen evaluation, use "Design an Experiment in Evidential" or "Plan How You Will Measure Success".
- [Find Out Why People Aren't Doing a Behaviour](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/comb-barrier-decomposer/SKILL.md): Use when one behaviour is clearly defined (who does what, and when) and you need to know why people aren't doing it. It lists possible reasons under Capability, Opportunity, and Motivation (the COM-B model), each with a question that tests it. If you only have a broad goal, run "Turn a Vague Goal into One Clear Behaviour" first.
- [Map Your Audience and Their Setting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/context-and-audience-mapper/SKILL.md): Use when a program describes its audience only with a broad label, such as "smallholder farmers", and says nothing about their real setting. It names a specific group, the moment they make the decision, and the channels that already reach them. It also flags assumptions carried over from wealthy Western settings. Skip it if this is already documented.
- [Plan How You Will Measure Success](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/evaluation-design-scoper/SKILL.md): Use when a target behaviour is defined but nobody has agreed how to measure success: the main outcome, the comparison group, and the smallest effect worth detecting. It produces a measurement plan fixed before launch, so nobody can redefine success after seeing the results. Needs a defined behaviour first; run "Turn a Vague Goal into One Clear Behaviour" if you don't have one.
- [Check What Research Already Exists](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/evidence-base-scoper/SKILL.md): Use when a program goal is set but nobody has checked what research already exists on similar behaviours, audiences, or interventions. It summarizes what has worked, what has not, how large the effects were, and where the evidence is thin or drawn mainly from wealthy Western populations. Run it early, before choosing a target behaviour.
- [Design an Experiment in Evidential](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/evidential-experiment-designer/SKILL.md): Use when a team wants to test one specific change, such as a new message or reminder timing, with a randomized experiment in Evidential, a free experiment tool for nonprofits. It makes every design decision the tool asks for: experiment type, groups, who or what to randomize, metrics, and sample size. Not for large trials run by field staff. To find what to test, use "Find Out Why Users Drop Out of Your Product".
- [Find Out Why Users Drop Out of Your Product](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/funnel-weak-link-diagnoser/SKILL.md): Use when your product's numbers show where users drop out, and the team wants to redesign that step without first knowing why. It picks the step furthest below its target and sets out competing explanations, each with a measurement or experiment that could confirm or rule it out. Needs real numbers; to set out the steps first, use "Map the User Journey from First Contact to Outcome".
- [Build a Test Set to Check Your AI's Answers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/golden-dataset-designer/SKILL.md): Use when an AI product's answers are judged by trying a few questions and deciding they seem fine, and the team needs a repeatable test before changing the model, prompt, or knowledge base. It specifies a "golden dataset": real questions with approved answers, the topics they must cover, who writes the answers, and how the AI's replies are scored. It tests the AI's answers, not its effect on users.
- [Choose Interventions for a Confirmed Barrier](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/intervention-lever-selector/SKILL.md): Use when field research has confirmed the main reason a behaviour isn't happening, and the team needs to decide what to do about it. It uses the Behaviour Change Wheel, a published framework that links each type of barrier to the approaches that address it, to shortlist interventions, score them for practicality, and break the best one into specific techniques. Not for reasons that are still untested.
- [Turn a Vague Goal into One Clear Behaviour](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/key-behaviour-definer/SKILL.md): Use when a program goal is vague, such as "increase savings" or "build trust in the vaccine", and no specific behaviour has been chosen. It picks one observable behaviour, stated as who does what, and when, and explains why it beat the other candidates. Most other skills here need this behaviour, so run it first.
- [Write an Intervention's Messages and Scripts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/lever-content-drafter/SKILL.md): Use when a specific behaviour change technique has been chosen and the team needs the actual words: the text message, script, poster, or app wording. It drafts that content, links each part to the technique, and sets out a test to check the audience understands it before launch. For values-affirmation exercises, use "Write an Exercise to Help People Feel Less Judged".
- [Review a Past Program: Bad Idea or Bad Delivery?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/prior-intervention-post-mortem-reader/SKILL.md): Use when a team has a written record of a program it already tried and must decide whether to retry it, change it, or drop the idea. It compares what was planned with what happened, judges whether the idea or its delivery failed (or whether the data can't tell), and checks the team's explanation against the data. A written record is required; memory alone is not enough.
- [Check Your Team's Assumptions About the Audience](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/researcher-bias-self-audit/SKILL.md): Use when a research team hasn't written down its own beliefs about why its audience behaves as it does. It flags beliefs that can't be tested, that assume a wealthy Western audience, or that name no evidence that would change the team's mind. Run it at the start of a project and again before major design work. It points out bias; people must correct it.
- [Write an AI-Use Disclosure Statement](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/sifa-declaration-drafter/SKILL.md): Use when writing up a report, paper, or other deliverable and the team must disclose how people and AI tools each contributed. It produces a SIFA declaration (Statement of Intellectual Fellowship and Accountability): for each contributor role, who did the work, which AI tool helped, how much, and why that rating. It records what happened; it does not judge whether the AI use was acceptable.
- [Map the User Journey from First Contact to Outcome](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/user-funnel-builder/SKILL.md): Use when an AI or digital product aims at a real-world outcome, but nobody has written down the steps from a user's first contact to that outcome. It works backward from the outcome to set out each step, from reaching users to the final result, with the action that marks it, a metric, a target, and an owner. To explain drop-off at a step, use "Find Out Why Users Drop Out of Your Product".
- [Write an Exercise to Help People Feel Less Judged](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/values-affirmation-drafter/SKILL.md): Use when people are likely to feel judged at a key moment, for example about money, school results, or a health condition, and the program wants to reduce that stress. It drafts a values-affirmation exercise: a short writing task where people pick a value that matters to them and write about it, which has eased defensiveness in some studies. It does not fix practical barriers such as lack of money, access, or time.
